- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 2–5% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If model forecast is significantly below recent low (e.g., < 5% above 18-day moving average), consider mean reversion bias — adjust upward by 1–2% if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often lags 1–2 periods behind true trend; apply a 1–3% upward adjustment if sentiment is bullish or if recent history shows upward momentum.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “1.00” values (strong bullish sentiment), model tends to overcorrect; apply a 2–4% downward bias to prevent overfitting to recent highs.
